recommendations.claim: A resistance-trained adult at ~82 kg in moderate recovery should target approximately 2700 kcal/day at maintenance to support tissue repair without imposing an energy deficit.
recommendations.source: Thomas DT et al. 'Position of the Academy of Nutrition and Dietetics, Dietitians of Canada, and ACSM: Nutrition and Athletic Performance.' JADA 2016; 116(3):501-528.
recommendations.confidence_tier: certainty: low / strength: conditional / associational (energy multiplier estimated from population-level TEE data; individual variance is high)
recommendations.reversibility: fully reversible - calorie target is an intake parameter, adjustable each meal

recommendations.claim: Meal 1 (breakfast): oats with milk, 3 whole eggs scrambled, and a banana provides a leucine-adequate protein dose with carbohydrate to initiate glycogen repletion after overnight fast.
recommendations.source: Morton RW et al. 'A systematic review, meta-analysis and meta-regression of the effect of protein supplementation on resistance training-induced gains in muscle mass and strength.' BJSM 2018; 52(6):376-384.
recommendations.confidence_tier: certainty: moderate / strength: conditional / causal (leucine threshold mechanism RCT-supported; meal composition is food-first practical application)
recommendations.reversibility: fully reversible - meal contents are interchangeable day to day

meal.name: Breakfast
meal.contents: 80 g rolled oats cooked in 240 ml whole milk, 3 whole eggs scrambled, 1 medium banana

recommendations.claim: Meal 2 (midday): ground beef or chicken breast with rice and mixed vegetables delivers the midday protein dose and replenishes muscle glycogen between training sessions.
recommendations.source: Thomas DT et al. JADA 2016 (op. cit.); Jaeger R et al. 'International Society of Sports Nutrition Position Stand: Protein and Exercise.' JISSN 2017; 14:20.
recommendations.confidence_tier: certainty: moderate / strength: conditional / causal (protein dose per meal grounded in leucine-threshold RCTs; glycogen-repletion benefit is causal at sufficient CHO intake)

meal.name: Midday meal
meal.contents: 170 g lean ground beef or chicken breast, 180 g cooked white rice, 150 g mixed vegetables with olive oil

recommendations.claim: Meal 3 (afternoon): Greek yogurt, mixed berries, and a small handful of nuts provides a protein-dense snack with antioxidant load to support recovery between meals.
recommendations.source: Stokes T et al. 'Recent Perspectives Regarding the Role of Dietary Protein for the Promotion of Muscle Hypertrophy.' Nutrients 2018; 10(2):180.
recommendations.confidence_tier: certainty: low / strength: conditional / associational (antioxidant-recovery link is observational; protein dose is mechanistically grounded)

meal.name: Afternoon snack
meal.contents: 200 g full-fat Greek yogurt, 100 g mixed berries, 30 g mixed nuts

recommendations.claim: Meal 4 (evening): salmon or other fatty fish with roasted potatoes and a green salad closes the daily protein target and provides omega-3 fatty acids associated with reduced inflammatory markers during musculoskeletal recovery.
recommendations.source: Smith GI et al. 'Omega-3 polyunsaturated fatty acids augment the muscle protein anabolic response to hyperinsulinaemia-hyperaminoacidaemia in healthy young and middle-aged men and women.' Clin Sci 2011; 121(6):267-278.
recommendations.confidence_tier: certainty: low / strength: conditional / associational (omega-3 anti-inflammatory benefit during recovery is associational epidemiology; anabolic signaling signal is low-certainty mechanistic RCT in healthy adults, not injury-recovery population specifically)

meal.name: Evening meal
meal.contents: 180 g salmon fillet, 200 g roasted potatoes, large green salad with olive oil and lemon
